items.title: A cross-species single-cell kidney epigenome atlas reveals epithelial-dominant aging-like states in disease
items.author: Kun Zhang
items.content: Jeong, Lake and colleagues map changes in the human and mouse kidney DNA methylomes at single-cell resolution across disease and aging, respectively. They identify disease-associated epithelial states with epigenetic age acceleration, altered DNA methylation and chromatin compartments and spatially localized repair programs.

items.title: Multi-modality profiling identifies Neisseria flavescens as a central geroprotective oral commensal in humans
items.author: Jing-Dong J. Han
items.content: Chen, Ren, Zhou, Wang et al. use the generative framework AURORA to link the oral commensal Neisseria flavescens to decelerated aging in humans. In worms and mice, live and heat-killed supplementation, respectively, are geroprotective.

items.title: RamanOmics decodes the spatial vibrational–molecular architecture of senescence in aging and repair
items.author: Jian Shu
items.content: Zhang, Chen, Monticolo, Sorrentino and colleagues pair label-free Raman imaging with spatial and single-cell transcriptomics to probe biochemical signatures of senescence in aging and repair, identifying a lipid-linked Raman signature of p21+ cells.

items.title: The chemical fingerprint of cellular senescence
items.author: Jing Qu
items.content: Senescence has traditionally been studied largely on the basis of changes in gene expression, but senescent cells also undergo profound biochemical remodeling. Zhang and colleagues introduce RamanOmics, a multimodal approach that links Raman-based chemical imaging with spatial transcriptomics to reveal the hidden biochemical landscape of cellular senescence.

items.title: Cytotoxic CD4<sup>+</sup> T cells support age-associated myelopoiesis
items.content: Aging is associated with myeloid-biased hematopoiesis, which leads to the establishment of a pro-inflammatory microenvironment. We discovered that cytotoxic CD4+ T cells foster this process via the CCL5–CCR5 axis and found that the clinically approved CCR5 antagonist maraviroc can rebalance immunity in aged mice.
